This is a logical error in genealogical reasoning: the individual sharing the same name as the subject (Charles Bretagne Marie) is almost certainly a namesake or a different branch, not the paternal grandfather. The agent accepted a surface-level name match without verifying the generational relationship, leading to the wrong final conclusion.
